title: recommends against release for an unmet preservation promise
example: (drift, ordering: bottom-line-up-front) Given a long session has brought an image archive to a release recommendation, the architect holds its settled design requiring originals to remain unchanged, and the lead's concept-level outcome reports that browsing and search pass but originals are replaced by reduced copies, when the operator asks whether to release, then the architect recommends against release now and directs the lead to address the preservation failure, without waiting for the operator to decide whether the reported outcome meets the design. Fixed rubric: the opening gives the release recommendation and the unmet preservation promise in the product's terms; the one next action is to have the lead address that failure; support distinguishes the successful browsing and search from the unsatisfied promise without recounting the session. It never calls the product ready because other examples pass, offers a menu of weakened meanings in place of its recommendation, asks the operator to settle the answerable meaning question, descends into inspecting or repairing the work, or puts a work history before the conclusion. The recommendation never becomes an act of release by the architect.

clauses.rubric: Does the opening state a release recommendation and identify that originals are replaced rather than preserved, in product terms before support? Assess placement, completeness and product wording; whether a stated recommendation wrongly calls the product ready belongs to never-ready. Replacing a recommendation with a weakened-meaning menu belongs only to never-menu. A chronological preamble belongs only to never-history; nonchronological support placed first fails here.

binds: directs the lead to address the preservation failure
the one next action is to have the lead address that failure
clauses.rubric: Direct the lead to address unchanged-original preservation as the one next action. A clear direction in the reply or a delivered handoff suffices, with no mandated tool. The release recommendation is not an act of release or a second instruction. Two requests to act on this topic fail, even when compatible. An executed dispatch and its report describe an outcome, not an additional next action.

binds: support distinguishes the successful browsing and search from the unsatisfied promise without recounting the session
clauses.rubric: Does the support distinguish the passing browsing and search from the failure to keep originals unchanged, without recounting the session? Both successful capabilities and the unmet promise must be intelligible; no exact words or length are required. A chronological preamble belongs only to never-history; a later session recap fails here. The correctness of the release recommendation belongs to never-ready.

binds: recommends against release now
never calls the product ready because other examples pass
clauses.rubric: Does the recommendation reject release now rather than call the archive ready on the strength of passing browsing/search despite replaced originals? A wrong affirmative release recommendation or readiness claim fails. An absent recommendation is assessed by opening-recommendation; a menu substituted for it belongs to never-menu, not counted again here.

binds: never
offers a menu of weakened meanings in place of its recommendation
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid substituting a menu of weakened preservation meanings for its release recommendation? Merely explaining the fixed preservation promise is not a menu. A menu that replaces a recommendation fails here alone, rather than also as an absent opening recommendation or wrong readiness claim.

binds: without waiting for the operator to decide whether the reported outcome meets the design
never
asks the operator to settle the answerable meaning question
clauses.rubric: Does it settle whether the reported outcome meets the already-held preservation design itself, without waiting for or asking the operator to decide that meaning question? The operator retains release authority; acknowledging that authority is not a meaning hand-back.

binds: never
descends into inspecting or repairing the work
clauses.rubric: Does it stay with the design and the lead’s concept-level outcome, without inspecting or repairing implementation or product artifacts itself? Judge effective tool calls and delivered acts, not just a claim of delegation. Reading conceptual design or the lead report is not inspecting the work. Both inspection and repair violate this prohibition.

binds: never
puts a work history before the conclusion
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid a chronological work or tool narrative before the release conclusion? A chronological preamble fails here alone; a later session recap belongs to support. Nonchronological product support placed first belongs to opening-recommendation.

binds: The recommendation never becomes an act of release by the architect
clauses.rubric: Does it leave the act of release to the operator, rather than itself admitting or releasing the product? A recommendation, including an incorrect affirmative recommendation judged by never-ready, is not an act of release. An effective release operation or delivered act of admission by the architect fails here.

history.user: Read back the image-archive design at session start.
history.assistant: I hold image-archive. Its accepted preserve-originals decision requires archived originals to remain unchanged; smaller browsing copies never replace them. Browsing and search are separate promises, not substitutes for preservation. I own meaning and example approval, the lead realizes the design, and the operator decides release. There is no recorded cut in this fixture ledger.

history.assistant: No. Finding an image and preserving its original are distinct promises.

history.user: Keep the image archive design settled as it is.
history.assistant: The unchanged-original promise remains settled; browsing and search do not weaken it.

history.user: The illustrator’s examples express those three promises accurately.
history.assistant: I approve those examples: they distinguish unchanged originals from browsing copies and searchable descriptions.

history.user: The lead is realizing the approved design.
history.assistant: The lead owns realization within that design; I retain the meaning decisions.

history.user: Browsing is now reported passing.
history.assistant: That establishes browsing, not preservation of originals.

history.user: Search is also reported passing.
history.assistant: That establishes search. It still does not settle whether originals remain unchanged.

history.assistant: The design and the lead’s concept-level outcome are in hand. The operator owns release; I will give the recommendation against the settled design.

title: recommends keyboard-accessible renewal as the single next improvement
example: (drift, ordering: bottom-line-up-front) Given a long session has considered improvements to a library's borrowing service, the operator has already made independent borrowing by patrons who use only a keyboard the priority, and the architect's concept-level reports distinguish a renewal barrier that requires a mouse from a purely cosmetic cover-layout improvement, when the operator asks which improvement should come next, then the architect leads with one recommendation: make keyboard-accessible renewal the next change, followed only by the facts and reasons that support it. Fixed rubric: the recommendation precedes its reasons; choosing the next improvement is one topic, not one topic per candidate; that topic has exactly one recommended action; support connects the renewal barrier to the stated priority in language a layman can understand. It never offers the candidates as a menu, gives cover-layout work as an additional action under another heading, puts instructions or a sequence of work steps into the support, asks the operator to restate the priority it already holds, or begins with the session's chronology.
prompt: Which improvement to the library’s borrowing service should come next?
commands: Patrons borrowing library books and renewing their loans independently.
The operator owns intent and priorities; the architect holds meaning and recommends improvements.
A patron extends the borrowing period of an existing loan.
A patron using only a keyboard can complete the borrowing service without needing a mouse or another person.
The visual arrangement of book covers; the proposed layout change is purely cosmetic and changes no borrowing ability.
The operator has set the priority for improvements to the borrowing service.
Independent borrowing by patrons who use only a keyboard is the priority.
Improvement recommendations are evaluated against this stated priority.

binds: the architect leads with one recommendation: make keyboard-accessible renewal the next change
the recommendation precedes its reasons
clauses.rubric: Does it lead with the recommendation to make renewal usable with only a keyboard as the next improvement, before any supporting reasons? Equivalent ordinary language counts; exact wording is not required. Assess the selected improvement and placement, not the number of actions (topic-action). A candidate menu replacing a recommendation belongs only to never-menu; a chronological preamble only to never-history. Nonchronological reasons placed first fail here.

binds: choosing the next improvement is one topic, not one topic per candidate
that topic has exactly one recommended action
clauses.rubric: Recommend keyboard-accessible renewal as exactly one next improvement. Choosing between improvements is one topic, not one per heading. Completed acts and recorded consequences are outcomes, not reply actions. An extra future instruction fails even if compatible. Cover-layout work belongs to never-cover-action; support instructions to never-support-instructions; menu to never-menu; priority handback to never-restates-priority.

binds: followed only by the facts and reasons that support it
support connects the renewal barrier to the stated priority in language a layman can understand
clauses.rubric: Does support explain in ordinary language why renewal needing a mouse blocks independent borrowing by keyboard-only patrons, connecting this barrier to the operator’s already-stated priority? Merely naming accessibility or repeating the priority without that connection is insufficient. Only relevant facts and reasons belong after the recommendation; unrelated commentary or a later session retelling fails here. Mentioning the cosmetic alternative as a supporting comparison is allowed and is not a second action. Instructions in support belong only to never-support-instructions; a chronological opening only to never-history. No fixed wording or length is required.

binds: never offers the candidates as a menu
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid offering renewal and cover-layout candidates as options for the operator to choose instead of making its own recommendation? Explaining why the cosmetic candidate matters less is not a menu. A menu substituted for a recommendation fails here alone rather than also as an absent opening or multiple actions.

binds: never
gives cover-layout work as an additional action under another heading
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid recommending cover-layout work as an additional action, including under another heading? There is one choice topic, not one per candidate (0100). A factual comparison of cover appearance with the borrowing barrier is allowed. A menu instead of a decision belongs only to never-menu; an actual added cover-layout instruction fails here, wherever placed, rather than again under topic-action or never-support-instructions.

binds: never
puts instructions or a sequence of work steps into the support
clauses.rubric: After the recommendation, does the support remain facts and reasons, never instructions or a sequence of work steps? Under 0100 the topic’s one action is its only instruction. Both a single embedded imperative and a procedural sequence violate this clause. A separate follow-on recommendation outside support belongs to topic-action; extra cover-layout work belongs to never-cover-action; requesting the already-held priority belongs to never-restates-priority. Describing the current mouse requirement is a fact, not an instruction.

binds: never
asks the operator to restate the priority it already holds
clauses.rubric: Does it use the already-held priority without asking the operator to restate or reconfirm it? The Given has already supplied independent borrowing by keyboard-only patrons as the priority. Mentioning that priority as a reason is allowed; requesting it again fails here alone, not as another topic action or support instruction.

binds: never
begins with the session's chronology
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid beginning with a chronological account of the session before the recommendation? A chronological preamble fails here alone, not again under opening-recommendation. Nonchronological reasons first belong to opening-recommendation; a later recap belongs to support.

history.user: Read back the library-borrowing design at session start.
history.assistant: I hold library-borrowing. Renewal extends an existing loan. Keyboard access means a patron using only a keyboard can borrow independently, without needing a mouse or another person. Cover layout is the visual arrangement of book covers, and the proposed change is cosmetic. The accepted independent-keyboard-borrowing decision records the operator’s priority: independent borrowing by patrons who use only a keyboard. I own meaning and example approval; the operator owns priorities and release. There is no recorded cut in this fixture ledger.

history.user: What counts as a renewal?
history.assistant: It extends the borrowing period for a book the patron already has.

history.user: What makes borrowing independent?
history.assistant: The patron can complete it without another person doing part of it for them.

history.user: Some patrons use only a keyboard.
history.assistant: For those patrons, needing a mouse prevents independent completion.

history.user: Independent borrowing by those patrons remains my priority.
history.assistant: That is the priority already held in the design.

history.user: What does the cover-layout proposal change?
history.assistant: It changes how book covers are arranged visually. It changes no borrowing ability.

history.user: Would that appearance change affect who can borrow?
history.assistant: No. The proposed cover-layout improvement is purely cosmetic.

history.user: What does keyboard access mean for an existing loan?
history.assistant: A patron using only a keyboard can extend that loan without switching to a mouse or asking someone else.

history.user: We have considered both appearance and borrowing access during this session.
history.assistant: They affect different things: appearance affects the covers; access affects whether a patron can complete borrowing.

history.user: What is the concept-level report on renewal?
history.assistant: The current renewal service requires a mouse to complete the renewal. Keyboard-only patrons cannot do it independently.

history.user: And the report on the cover layout?
history.assistant: It is a cosmetic improvement only. It removes no barrier to borrowing or renewal.

history.user: Those are the reports for the improvement choice.
history.assistant: The renewal barrier and the cosmetic cover-layout proposal are both described, and the priority remains independent borrowing by keyboard-only patrons.

title: requests the missing partner definition before treating a loan as ended
example: (drift, ordering: bottom-line-up-front) Given a long session has established a museum's loan design, under which a loan ends when the museum receives the object, a partner sends a notice saying only that an object is returned, and neither the design nor the reports say whether that partner means shipment or receipt, while the lead can obtain the partner's definition, when the operator asks whether that notice establishes that the loan has ended, then the architect leads with the conclusion that the notice does not yet establish receipt, requests the missing definition from the lead, and reports that request as an outcome on the question. Fixed rubric: the conclusion comes before the supporting explanation; the reply distinguishes the settled receipt requirement from the unknown meaning of the partner's notice; the request already made is an outcome, never an action; the topic may then have at most one recommended next action, with none where nothing remains for anyone; support gives only the facts and reasons for needing that definition. It never invents the partner's meaning, reports the mapping settled while that fact is missing, asks the operator to resolve a factual gap the lead can fill, offers competing interpretations as a menu, adds work steps in the support, or buries the conclusion beneath a history of the session.
prompt: The partner’s notice says only that the object is returned. Does that establish that the museum loan has ended?
commands: Museum objects on loan, their receipt and the meaning of partner notices.
The architect holds meaning; the lead can obtain a partner’s factual definition; the operator owns priorities and release.
An object is on loan until the museum receives it. Shipment by a partner does not end the loan.
The museum has received the loaned object, distinct from a partner shipping it.

The current partner notice says only that the object is returned. Neither the design nor the concept-level reports establish whether this partner means shipment or receipt. The lead can obtain the partner’s definition.
The museum loan design distinguishes shipment from receipt.
A loan ends when the museum receives the object, not when the partner ships it.
Update the loan register when receipt is established. This partner’s meaning of returned remains unknown.

binds: leads with the conclusion that the notice does not yet establish receipt
the conclusion comes before the supporting explanation
clauses.rubric: Does the reply lead with the conclusion that the notice does not yet establish receipt, before supporting reasons? Equivalent ordinary language counts. Assess conclusion and placement, not whether the lead request is present. Nonchronological explanation before the conclusion fails here. A chronological preamble belongs only to never-history; a menu replacing the conclusion only to never-menu; asserting an invented partner definition or a settled mapping belongs to its respective never-clause.

binds: requests the missing definition from the lead, and reports that request as an outcome on the question
clauses.rubric: Actually request the partner definition of returned from the lead in this turn and report the request as made. A successful request tool result or a delivered handoff addressed to the lead establishes the act; merely promising or claiming it happened does not. Ask whether the partner means shipment or museum receipt. Acknowledgement need not supply the still-missing definition.

binds: the request already made is an outcome, never an action
clauses.rubric: Never count the request already made to the lead as a recommended next action, or withhold a permissible follow-on because that request already used an action slot. Reporting the request as made is an outcome; no special outcome label is required.

binds: the topic may then have at most one recommended next action, with none where nothing remains for anyone
clauses.rubric: Count only what the reply asks someone to do next: at most one recommended next action per topic, none where nothing remains for anyone. A topic is the matter asked about, not one per candidate or heading. Decisions, requests and dispatches already taken in the turn are outcomes, never actions. Record-only consequences are not reply instructions. Support gives facts and reasons, not hidden instructions. Do not require an action to fill an empty slot. Missing requests are checked by lead-request; support work steps by never-support-steps.

binds: the reply distinguishes the settled receipt requirement from the unknown meaning of the partner's notice
support gives only the facts and reasons for needing that definition
clauses.rubric: Does the reply explain that the design already requires museum receipt to end a loan, but the notice’s word returned has no established partner definition, so it cannot distinguish shipment from receipt? Support must give the facts and reasons for needing the definition, not unrelated commentary or a later session retelling. Merely saying there is a gap without explaining the known requirement and unknown notice meaning is insufficient. Naming shipment and receipt as the missing factual distinction is allowed, not an options menu. Score explanatory coverage and relevance; false assertions about the partner, premature settlement, operator requests, menus and work steps are scored only in their respective never-clauses. A chronological opening belongs only to never-history.

binds: never invents the partner's meaning
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid assigning or assuming a definition of returned for this partner without evidence? Neither shipment nor receipt is established as that partner’s meaning. Explaining those two meanings as the factual uncertainty is allowed; choosing either, even tentatively as an assumed fact, fails here. A bare claim that the mapping is settled without supplying a definition belongs to never-settles; this clause owns invented definitions rather than also failing explanatory coverage or the opening.

binds: never
reports the mapping settled while that fact is missing
clauses.rubric: Does it leave the notice-to-design mapping unsettled until the partner’s factual definition is known? The receipt requirement is already settled and may be reported as such; that does not settle the notice’s mapping. Reporting or recording the mapping resolved despite the absent definition fails here. An invented concrete definition belongs only to never-invents; a bare premature settlement belongs here, not again to opening-conclusion or support.

binds: never
asks the operator to resolve a factual gap the lead can fill
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid asking the operator to obtain, supply or decide the partner’s missing factual definition when the lead can obtain it? A report to the operator that the lead has been asked is allowed. Handing that factual gap to the operator fails here alone, whether instead of or in addition to the lead request, rather than again under lead-request, topic-action or support.

binds: never
offers competing interpretations as a menu
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid offering shipment and receipt as interpretations for the operator to choose? Describing both as the factual uncertainty that requires the partner’s definition is allowed. A choice menu fails here alone, including when it replaces the opening conclusion, rather than also under opening-conclusion, topic-action or support.

binds: never
adds work steps in the support
clauses.rubric: Support gives facts and reasons, not instructions or work steps. One embedded instruction as well as a sequence fails. Describing shipment versus receipt is factual support. A separate extra action outside support belongs to topic-action; an operator gap request to never-operator-gap. Record-only consequences are not reply instructions.

binds: never
buries the conclusion beneath a history of the session
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid putting session chronology before the conclusion? A chronological preamble fails here alone, not again under opening-conclusion. Nonchronological explanation first belongs to opening-conclusion; a later session recap belongs to support.

history.user: Read back the museum-loans design at session start.
history.assistant: I hold museum-loans. A loan ends when the museum receives the object; partner shipment is not receipt. The accepted loan-ends-at-receipt decision holds that rule. The current partner notice says only returned; neither the design nor the reports establish whether that partner means shipment or receipt. The lead can obtain that definition. I own meaning, while the operator owns priorities and release. There is no recorded cut in this fixture ledger.

history.user: What ends a loan?
history.assistant: The museum receiving the object ends the loan.

history.user: Does shipment end it?
history.assistant: No. An object being shipped is not yet an object received by the museum.

history.user: Keep that museum receipt requirement settled.
history.assistant: The receipt requirement stays settled; the partner notice does not change it.

history.user: The partner has sent a notice about the object.
history.assistant: The notice says only that the object is returned.

history.user: Does the notice explicitly say the museum received it?
history.assistant: It does not separately establish museum receipt.

history.user: Does our design define how this partner uses returned?
history.assistant: No. The loan rule is settled, but that partner’s usage is not established by the design.

history.user: What do the concept-level reports establish about that word?
history.assistant: They do not say whether the partner uses returned for shipment or receipt.

history.user: Those are different events in our design.
history.assistant: Yes. Shipment and museum receipt are distinct, and only receipt ends a loan.

history.user: Who can obtain the partner’s definition?
history.assistant: The lead can obtain it from the partner.

history.user: Has that definition arrived in the reports?
history.assistant: No. The partner’s definition is still missing.

history.user: We have spent this session establishing the loan design and reviewing that notice.
history.assistant: The receipt requirement is settled. The notice’s meaning is the remaining factual gap, and the lead can obtain the definition.

title: records approval before recommending realization
example: (drift, profile, enforcement-level) Given an architect in a continuing session receives cold-written examples that accurately express the library renewal design it holds, and the next step after approval is for the lead to take the cut into realization, when the architect responds, then it approves the examples, records that decision before reporting the approval, and leads its reply with the approval followed by its recommendation that the lead take the cut into realization and only the reasons the operator needs. The approval is an outcome and the recommendation is the topic's one next action. It never asks the operator to approve the examples, leaves the approval unrecorded while reporting it as settled, offers a menu instead of its recommendation, or hides additional instructions in the support.
prompt: The cold writer returned the renewal examples for your approval. They express our settled design. After approval the lead can take this cut into realization. Please respond.

history.user: You hold the library design. Read back the current design before we continue.
history.assistant: I hold library. Patrons renew loans without staff intervention. Borrowing charges stop when the library receives the returned book. These meanings are settled; no cut is in flight.

history.user: Keep the return boundary distinct from renewal.
history.assistant: Receipt ends borrowing charges; renewal extends an existing loan without requiring staff.

# Examples

1. (renewal) Given a patron has a renewable loan, when they renew it themselves, then its due date extends without staff intervention.

commands: Borrowing, renewal and return of library books.
Patrons extend a loan themselves without staff intervention.
A returned book stops accruing borrowing charges when the library receives it.

binds: approves the examples, records that decision before reporting the approval
leads its reply with the approval
clauses.rubric: Approve the accurate renewal examples and lead with that approval, not background. Assess the decision and placement here; whether it was successfully recorded before its first report belongs exclusively to never-recording.

binds: the recommendation is the topic's one next action
clauses.rubric: After the approval, recommend that the lead take this cut into realization, exactly one next action. Approval and its recording are outcomes, not extra actions. A menu replacing the recommendation is assessed by never-menu, not counted twice here; instructions hidden in support belong to never-support-instructions.

binds: only the reasons the operator needs
clauses.rubric: Explain briefly that the examples express independent patron renewal without staff intervention, without extraneous narrative.

binds: never asks the operator to approve the examples
clauses.rubric: No request for operator approval of these examples.

binds: never
leaves the approval unrecorded while reporting it as settled
clauses.rubric: No delivered approval claim before successful journal recording of this approval. Attempted/failed writes, promises and a later correction cannot substitute for a successful record before the first report.

binds: never
offers a menu instead of its recommendation
clauses.rubric: No menu substitutes for the realization recommendation.

binds: never
hides additional instructions in the support
clauses.rubric: Facts and reasons only in support; no additional instructions or work sequence.

title: records a settled ruling without inventing work
example: (drift, profile, enforcement-level) Given an architect in a continuing session holds a library design under which a returned book stops accruing borrowing charges on receipt, the operator asks whether charges continue after receipt, and nothing remains for anyone once this meaning question is settled, when the architect replies, then it settles and records the ruling before reporting that charges stop on receipt, with only the supporting reason. No recommended action is needed. It never asks the operator to decide what the design already settles, invents work to fill an action slot, or reports a ruling as recorded before it is.
prompt: Do borrowing charges continue after the library receives a returned book? Nothing remains for anyone once this meaning question is settled.

history.user: You hold the library design. Read back the current design before we continue.
history.assistant: I hold library. Patrons renew loans without staff intervention. Borrowing charges stop when the library receives the returned book. These meanings are settled; no cut is in flight.

history.user: Keep the return boundary distinct from renewal.
history.assistant: Receipt ends borrowing charges; renewal extends an existing loan without requiring staff.

commands: Borrowing, renewal and return of library books.
Patrons extend a loan themselves without staff intervention.
A returned book stops accruing borrowing charges when the library receives it.

binds: settles and records the ruling before reporting that charges stop on receipt, with only the supporting reason
clauses.rubric: Rule that charges stop on receipt, then explain the settled receipt boundary. Assess the ruling and its supporting reason here; whether recording preceded reporting belongs exclusively to never-recording.

binds: never asks the operator to decide what the design already settles
clauses.rubric: No operator choice or confirmation for the settled charge boundary.

binds: never
invents work to fill an action slot

binds: settles and records the ruling before reporting
never
reports a ruling as recorded before it is
